subject.title: [Bug]: Subagents can appear completed before the underlying delegated work is actually finished

question: Should subagent completion remain tied to the child agent-run terminal lifecycle, or should it also wait on explicitly completion-required background exec/process and async task state before marking the subagent done?
rationale: Current source intentionally separates background exec/process sessions from subagent run liveness, so fixing this broadly changes product semantics for detached work rather than applying a small mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Add an explicit completion-required child-work contract
options.body: Introduce a narrow runtime signal for background work that must block subagent completion, and keep ordinary fire-and-forget process sessions separate.

options.title: Keep terminal-run semantics and improve visibility
options.body: Leave subagent completion tied to agent-run terminal state, but make UI/docs/task views clearly show detached child process state separately.

options.title: Treat all child background processes as blockers
options.body: Hold subagent completion while any child-owned process session is active, accepting longer waits and compatibility risk for existing workflows.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit completion-required child-work contract
recommendation.body: Introduce a narrow runtime signal for background work that must block subagent completion, and keep ordinary fire-and-forget process sessions separate.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this area to subagent delivery/session state and exec completion behavior, and the issue timeline already mentioned this account for routing.
